{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "feasible",
    "answerable": [
      "Elevation gradient of peak (annual maximum) SWE across the Wenatchee basin using columns co-located with the 5 SNOTEL stations",
      "Model-vs-observation skill for peak SWE and SWE timing at each SNOTEL station (bias, RMSE, peak-date offset, melt-out date)",
      "Interannual variability of peak SWE 1980-2018 at each elevation"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Fully spatially-distributed basin SWE fields (only 5 point columns; no dense snow courses to validate spatial interpolation)",
      "Sub-station-scale terrain/aspect controls on SWE (single-column ELM has no lateral snow redistribution or shading)",
      "Attribution beyond elevation (only elevation offered as candidate driver; wind redistribution/canopy interception effects unverified without additional obs)"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 5,
  "n_justification": "One column per available SNOTEL station so simulated peak SWE can be directly compared to each observation, and the 5 columns collectively span the basin elevation gradient (~1000-1900 m) enabling the elevation-vs-peak-SWE relationship to be quantified. Adding columns would have no validating observations.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "fish_lake_low", "lat": 47.555, "lon": -120.760, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "trinity_mid", "lat": 48.028, "lon": -120.940, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "stevens_pass_mid", "lat": 47.745, "lon": -121.090, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "grouse_camp_high", "lat": 47.900, "lon": -120.870, "soil_texture": "gravelly_loam"},
    {"id": "pope_ridge_high", "lat": 47.680, "lon": -120.480, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "39",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1980-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "H2OSNO",
      "SNOWDP",
      "SNOW",
      "RAIN",
      "FSNO",
      "QSNOMELT",
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QOVER",
      "TSA",
      "TG",
      "FSDS",
      "TBOT",
      "SNOWLIQ",
      "SNOWICE",
      "FSA",
      "FIRA"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "single-column ELM (I-compset, satellite phenology or BGC-off)",
    "GSWP3/CRUNCEP-style meteorological forcing 1980-2018 with elevation-adjusted downscaling to each column",
    "SNOTEL SWE data ingestion for validation (5 stations)",
    "surface dataset with per-column elevation, PFT, and soil texture"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Column lat/lon and elevations are set to the actual SNOTEL station coordinates; forcing is lapse-rate downscaled to station elevation to preserve the elevation gradient signal",
    "Peak SWE defined as the annual maximum daily H2OSNO for each water year (Oct 1-Sep 30)",
    "First 2 water years (1980-1981) treated as snowpack spin-up and excluded from skill statistics",
    "Vegetation held at present-day evergreen-needleleaf/subalpine mix; no land-cover change over the period",
    "Monthly plus daily history output; daily resolution used for peak-SWE and melt-out timing comparison against SNOTEL",
    "No lateral snow redistribution, avalanching, or sub-grid aspect effects represented (single-column limitation)"
  ]
}

answerable: Elevation gradient of peak (annual maximum) SWE across the Wenatchee basin using columns co-located with the 5 SNOTEL stations
Model-vs-observation skill for peak SWE and SWE timing at each SNOTEL station (bias, RMSE, peak-date offset, melt-out date)
Interannual variability of peak SWE 1980-2018 at each elevation
not_answerable: Fully spatially-distributed basin SWE fields (only 5 point columns; no dense snow courses to validate spatial interpolation)
Sub-station-scale terrain/aspect controls on SWE (single-column ELM has no lateral snow redistribution or shading)
Attribution beyond elevation (only elevation offered as candidate driver; wind redistribution/canopy interception effects unverified without additional obs)

parsed.n_justification: One column per available SNOTEL station so simulated peak SWE can be directly compared to each observation, and the 5 columns collectively span the basin elevation gradient (~1000-1900 m) enabling the elevation-vs-peak-SWE relationship to be quantified. Adding columns would have no validating observations.
requires_capabilities: single-column ELM (I-compset, satellite phenology or BGC-off)
GSWP3/CRUNCEP-style meteorological forcing 1980-2018 with elevation-adjusted downscaling to each column
SNOTEL SWE data ingestion for validation (5 stations)
surface dataset with per-column elevation, PFT, and soil texture
assumptions: Column lat/lon and elevations are set to the actual SNOTEL station coordinates; forcing is lapse-rate downscaled to station elevation to preserve the elevation gradient signal
Peak SWE defined as the annual maximum daily H2OSNO for each water year (Oct 1-Sep 30)
First 2 water years (1980-1981) treated as snowpack spin-up and excluded from skill statistics
Vegetation held at present-day evergreen-needleleaf/subalpine mix; no land-cover change over the period
Monthly plus daily history output; daily resolution used for peak-SWE and melt-out timing comparison against SNOTEL
No lateral snow redistribution, avalanching, or sub-grid aspect effects represented (single-column limitation)
